note: Follows 2.2 (levels, sublevels, orbitals) and sets up 2.4 (valence electrons, ions). Notation convention: filling order, e.g. [Ar] 4s2 3d6, written with raised numbers. Required through Kr (Z = 36). Cr and Cu are the only exceptions taught. Every configuration and orbital diagram on these slides is checked by scripts/build_diagram_u02_s02.3_configurations.py. 50-minute period; the last 5 minutes are cleanup/reset.

fields.headline:
2.3
Electron
Configurations
fields.subhead: Write configurations and orbital diagrams through krypton, and catch mistakes in them.

imageSubjects.section: a long row of numbered wooden mail slots in a dim hallway, a few holding envelopes

fields.headline: Where Are Oxygen's Electrons?
fields.subhead: The periodic table gives you the count: 8. Today you write where each one sits.
fields.keyq: Oxygen has 8 electrons. Do all 8 have the same energy?

imageSubjects.concept: an apartment building at dusk with a few lit windows on different floors

fields.headline: Reading an Electron Configuration
fields.subhead: Take 2p^{4} apart one piece at a time.
fields.k1_b:
The big number in front.

2p^{4} is in level 2.
fields.k2_b:
The letter: s, p, d, or f.

2p^{4} is in the p sublevel.
fields.mustwrite: A configuration lists where the electrons sit. Ground state means the lowest-energy arrangement.

imageSubjects.aside: a printed periodic table with oxygen's cell circled in pencil

fields.headline: The Order Electrons Fill In
fields.subhead: Read each arrow from top right to bottom left, then start the next arrow.
fields.a1_b: The lowest-energy open orbital fills first.
fields.a3_b: 4s fills before 3d, in K and Ca.

fields.headline: Pauli: Two per Orbital, Opposite Spins
fields.subhead: Up and down arrows are spin labels, not electrons orbiting opposite ways.
fields.a1_b: One orbital holds at most 2 electrons.
fields.a2_b: If there are two, their spins are opposite.
fields.a3_b: Two per orbital, not two per sublevel.

fields.headline: Hund's Rule: Singles Before Pairs
fields.subhead: Equal-energy orbitals, like the three 2p boxes, each get one electron first.
fields.a1_b: Singles first, all pointing the same way.
fields.a2_b: Its 2p^{3} is three single electrons: 3 unpaired.

fields.headline: Reading an Orbital Diagram
fields.subhead: One box per orbital. Nitrogen has 7 electrons, so 7 arrows.
fields.a2_b: Draw the up arrow first in every box.
fields.a3_b: The raised number counts the arrows.

fields.headline: Writing a Configuration
fields.subhead: The same four steps, for every element.
fields.s1_b: Atomic number is the electron count.
fields.s4_b: The raised numbers must total Z.

imageSubjects.band: a periodic table wall chart photographed at a shallow angle

fields.headline: Example: Oxygen
fields.subhead: Copy the setup, not just the answer.
fields.problem: Write the longhand configuration and the orbital diagram for oxygen.
fields.g2_b:
Longhand configuration
Orbital diagram
Unpaired electrons
fields.mustwrite: Always check that the raised numbers add up to Z.

imageSubjects.aside: a small cylinder of oxygen gas with a regulator, on a lab cart

fields.headline: Oxygen, Worked
fields.subhead: Order first. Then singles before pairs in the 2p boxes.

fields.headline: Longhand: N, Cl, and Ca
fields.subhead: Calcium stops at 4s^{2}. The 3d sublevel stays empty until scandium.
fields.mustwrite: The raised numbers add up to the atomic number, every time.

imageSubjects.aside: period 3 of a periodic table wall chart, lit from the side

fields.headline: Noble-Gas Shorthand
fields.subhead: Replace the filled inner core with a noble gas in brackets.
fields.mustwrite: Use the noble gas from the previous period. Cl is in period 3, so its core is [Ne].

imageSubjects.concept: a neon sign tube glowing orange-red in a dark window

fields.headline: Example: Iron
fields.subhead: Longhand, shorthand, and the unpaired count.
fields.problem: Write longhand and shorthand for iron. How many unpaired electrons?
fields.mustwrite: Fill 4s before 3d. We write 4s ahead of 3d.

imageSubjects.aside: a rusted iron nail on a white bench

fields.headline: Iron, Worked
fields.subhead: Argon is the core. Then 4s, then 3d.
fields.mustwrite: Fe is [Ar] 4s^{2} 3d^{6}. One pair and 4 singles in the 3d boxes.

fields.headline: Two Exceptions: Cr and Cu
fields.subhead: Learn both. The rules predict 4s^{2} for each, and the measurements disagree.
fields.a3_b: Half-full and full 3d are extra stable.

fields.headline: Checking a Configuration
fields.subhead: Run these four checks in order.
fields.s1_b: Do the raised numbers add up to Z?
fields.s3_b: Singles first. Pairs have opposite spins.
fields.s4_b: Previous noble gas? Is it Cr or Cu?

imageSubjects.band: a teacher's red pen resting on a page of student work

fields.headline: Example: Spot the Mistake
fields.subhead: Each was written as a ground state.
fields.problem: Each of these is wrong. Name the rule or fact it breaks.
fields.mustwrite: Add the electrons first. If the total is not Z, stop there.

imageSubjects.aside: a page of student work with a few lines circled in red pen

fields.headline: Spot the Mistake, Worked
fields.subhead: Four different problems, four different checks.
fields.f1_b:
(a) 10 electrons. O has 8.
(b) 4s fills before 3d.
(c) [Ne] 4s^{2} totals 12.
(d) Rules fit, atom does not.
fields.work:
Breaks:
(a) the count
(b) Aufbau
(c) the core
(d) the real Cr
fields.mustwrite: Cr follows the rules on paper, but the measured ground state is [Ar] 4s^{1} 3d^{5}.

imageSubjects.data: a pencil resting on a page of crossed-out electron counts

fields.headline: Check Yourself
fields.subhead: Work all three in your notes before we compare.
fields.k2_b: Write the shorthand and sketch the 3p boxes.
fields.k3_b: Write the actual shorthand. Say why it is an exception.
fields.mustwrite: Show the electron sum for each one. If it is not Z, find the error.
